documents.title: Emergency Department Record - Trauma Center
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRAUMA CENTER - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 02/07/2026 09:40 by ALS ambulance. Trauma activation.

HPI: 24 y/o M, unrestrained driver, car versus tree head-on at high speed per EMS. Intubated in the trauma bay on arrival to protect his airway. GCS 4 (E1 V1 M2). History from EMS and family by phone: ADHD and seasonal allergies.
Home meds per family: methylphenidate extended-release 20 mg each morning; cetirizine 10 mg daily if needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: T&A at age 8; ORIF right distal radius at 16.
FH (per mother): father hypertension and hyperlipidemia; mother major depressive disorder; older brother ADHD.
SH: construction laborer; quit cigarettes roughly 18 months back (had been 1/2 ppd); 2-3 beers on weekends.

Vitals on the ventilator: BP 122/78, HR 86, SpO2 98%.
Exam: No scalp laceration, step-off or other sign of external head injury. Pupils equal and reactive. No lateralizing findings. Remainder of trauma survey per trauma flowsheet.

Data: CBC and chemistries unremarkable. Serum ethanol and urine toxicology negative. Noncontrast head CT: no hemorrhage, mass or fracture. EEG at bedside: background preserved, no electrographic seizures. MRI brain to follow once stable.

ED course / MDM: Severe closed head injury by exam with a CT that does not explain his coma. Neurosurgery consulted and saw him in the department. Admitted to the neurosurgical ICU.

Disposition: admitted, critical condition.
[Received by fax 03/18/2026 in response to records request]

events.reason: severe traumatic brain injury after motor vehicle collision

reports.text: Indication: TBI, follow-up after admission. Comparison: head CT from this morning. Findings: Diffuse effacement of the cerebral sulci and basal cisterns with loss of gray-white differentiation consistent with diffuse cerebral edema. No focal parenchymal lesion. No intracranial hemorrhage. No midline shift. Calvarium intact.
reports.conclusion: Diffuse cerebral edema without a focal lesion.

reports.text: Indication: persistent coma after high-speed MVC with a nonfocal CT. Technique: multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain without contrast, including diffusion-weighted and susceptibility-weighted imaging. Findings: Pattern of diffuse axonal injury. No intracranial hemorrhage, including on susceptibility imaging. No extra-axial collection. Diffuse cerebral swelling as on CT. No hydrocephalus.

documents.title: Neurosurgery ICU Admission Note
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
NEUROSURGICAL ICU - ADMISSION NOTE
Date of service: 02/07/2026

24-year-old man brought up from our ED this afternoon after a high-speed crash; he was the unrestrained driver and the car hit a tree. Arrived intubated; on propofol for sedation and fentanyl for pain control.
Background: ADHD, combined type, and seasonal allergic rhinitis. Home medications methylphenidate ER 20 mg every morning and cetirizine 10 mg as needed - both held on admission. NKDA. Prior T&A (age 8) and right distal radius ORIF (age 16). Father: hypertension, hyperlipidemia. Mother: major depressive disorder. Brother: ADHD. Construction laborer, former smoker (quit about 18 months ago, half a pack a day), weekend beer.

Vitals: BP 110/70, HR 92, RR 14 (ventilator), SpO2 98% on FiO2 0.50.
Exam: GCS 6. Pupils equal and reactive. No external head trauma.
Labs: Na 138, K 4.1, Cl 100, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 110.
Imaging: repeat noncontrast head CT shows diffuse cerebral edema without a focal lesion.

Assessment: Severe TBI with diffuse traumatic cerebral edema and elevated intracranial pressure. Comatose, ventilator dependent.
Plan: Intraparenchymal ICP monitor placed at bedside; pressures elevated. Head of bed 30 degrees, sedation and analgesia as above, hypertonic saline for ICP control with sodium goals. MRI brain when safe to travel. Serial neuro checks. Home medications held.

documents.title: Neurosurgery ICU Progress Note
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
NEUROSURGICAL ICU - PROGRESS NOTE
Date of service: 02/09/2026 (hospital day 3)

Still comatose; he has not woken over the first 48 hours. Remains intubated on propofol and fentanyl.
Overnight and this morning: recurrent spells of tachycardia to 130, blood pressure surging to 190/110, respiratory rate up to 30, temperature to 38.9 C, with drenching sweats.
Exam during a spell: pupils dilated, tone increased, extensor posturing. Between spells GCS 7.
Labs: sodium 147 on hypertonic saline; remainder of chemistry and counts within normal limits.
MRI brain today: diffuse axonal injury; no hemorrhage.

Assessment:
1. Diffuse axonal injury.
2. Paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity - spells fit the pattern.
3. Traumatic cerebral edema with elevated ICP - on hyperosmolar therapy.
4. Coma; ventilator dependent.
Plan: Start propranolol 20 mg per tube every 6 hours and gabapentin 300 mg per tube three times a day. Continue sedation and ICP management. Home methylphenidate and cetirizine remain on hold.

documents.title: ICU Transfer Summary
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
TRANSFER SUMMARY - NEUROSURGICAL ICU TO INPATIENT BRAIN INJURY REHABILITATION
Admitted 02/07/2026. Transferred 03/06/2026.

Diagnoses: diffuse axonal injury; traumatic cerebral edema with elevated intracranial pressure; paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity; coma; dependence on mechanical ventilation. Background ADHD (combined type) and seasonal allergic rhinitis.

Course: Unrestrained driver in a high-speed crash; GCS 4 in our ED with a head CT that showed no bleed or fracture. Repeat CT the same day showed diffuse cerebral edema and an ICP monitor confirmed raised pressure, managed with sedation (propofol), analgesia (fentanyl), positioning and hypertonic saline. MRI on day 3 showed diffuse axonal injury without hemorrhage. Sympathetic storming began on day 3 and settled after propranolol and gabapentin were started. Tracheostomy and percutaneous gastrostomy tube placed 02/19/2026 for prolonged ventilation and coma. Weaned off the ventilator to trach collar by 03/02/2026; propofol and fentanyl were stopped before then.

Status at transfer: opens eyes spontaneously; not yet consistently following commands. Trach collar. Fed by gastrostomy tube.
Labs week of transfer: CBC and basic chemistry normal.

Medications at transfer: propranolol 20 mg per tube every 6 hours; gabapentin 300 mg per tube three times daily. Held: methylphenidate ER 20 mg, cetirizine 10 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Transferred to an inpatient brain injury rehabilitation unit.
[Received by fax 05/27/2026 after second request; copied to PCP]

Methylphenidate and cetirizine on hold. Nothing from rehab yet. Will go over all of it when he is back with us.
